cards.front: What are the key supervisory duties of a registered principal at a member firm?
cards.back: Approving new accounts; approving margin and options accounts; approving/reviewing communications with the public; reviewing trading activity; hiring and training representatives; and responding to written customer complaints.

cards.front: What is the minimum number of registered principals a member firm must employ?
cards.back: At least two registered principals, unless the firm is a sole proprietorship.

cards.front: Customer complaint (FINRA definition)
cards.back: Any written statement by a customer (or person acting on the customer's behalf) alleging a grievance arising from or in connection with a securities transaction. Written includes electronic communications such as email.

cards.front: How often must member firms report written customer complaints to FINRA, and how long must copies be retained?
cards.back: A report listing all written complaints must be filed with FINRA within 15 days after the end of each calendar quarter. Copies of complaints must be retained for 4 years after resolution.

cards.front: Who at a member firm is responsible for responding to written customer complaints?
cards.back: A registered principal — all written complaints must be directed to a principal for action.

cards.front: What are the two components of FINRA's continuing education requirement, and who designs each?
cards.back: Firm Element — designed by the member firm (annual training plan tailored to its business and personnel). Regulatory Element — content determined by FINRA.

cards.front: Under current FINRA rules, how often must a registered person complete the Regulatory Element of continuing education?
cards.back: Annually. Under FINRA Rule 1240 (amended effective 3/15/2022), the Regulatory Element must be completed each year by December 31, within 120 days of the registration anniversary date. (This replaced the old 2nd/5th/8th/11th-year cycle.)

cards.front: Who must complete the Firm Element of continuing education, and by what deadline?
cards.back: All registered persons who have direct contact with the public. It must be completed at least annually, with a year-end deadline of December 31 (firms may set an earlier internal deadline). Failure can result in suspension of the representative's license.

cards.front: What happens if a registered person fails to complete the Regulatory Element within the required period?
cards.back: FINRA will deactivate (suspend) the person's registration until the Regulatory Element requirements are completed.

cards.front: Under the Maintaining Qualifications Program (MQP), how long may a terminated registered person extend the 2-year requalification window?
cards.back: Up to 5 years, by electing into the MQP through FinPro and completing the annual Regulatory Element CE during that period.

cards.front: Under FINRA Rule 3270, what must a registered representative do before engaging in an outside business activity (OBA)?
cards.back: Provide prior written notice to the employing member firm. Notice is required whether or not compensation is received, except that passive investments and certain activities done through the firm are excluded.

cards.front: A registered rep wants to teach a paid evening business class at a community college. Does she need to notify her broker-dealer?
cards.back: Yes. Because she is receiving outside compensation for work outside her BD, she must provide prior written notice to the firm under FINRA Rule 3270 (OBA rule) before beginning the activity.

cards.front: A registered rep wants to volunteer (uncompensated) as a little league coach. Must she notify her firm under the OBA rule?
cards.back: No. With no compensation and no business activity involved, prior written notice is not required for this volunteer activity.

cards.front: Private securities transaction (selling away)
cards.back: Any sale of securities outside an associated person's regular business and outside the employing member firm. Governed by FINRA Rule 3280.

cards.front: What must an associated person do before participating in a private securities transaction?
cards.back: Provide prior written notice to the employer describing the proposed transaction in detail, the associated person's proposed role, and whether compensation has been or will be received.

cards.front: How does the firm's response to a private securities transaction differ depending on whether the rep will be compensated?
cards.back: With compensation: the firm must approve or disapprove. If approved, the firm must record the transaction on its books and supervise it as if its own. If disapproved, the rep may not participate. Without compensation: the firm must acknowledge the notice in writing and may impose conditions or prohibit participation entirely.

cards.front: An RR sells private placement interests to outside investors without notifying her firm. What violation has occurred?
cards.back: Selling away — a violation of FINRA Rule 3280 (private securities transactions). The RR failed to provide prior written notice to her employing member firm.

cards.front: What is the annual dollar limit on gifts a BD or its associated persons may give to employees of another member firm?
cards.back: $100 per person, per year. The gift must not be conditioned on sales and must be permitted by the recipient's employing firm.

cards.front: What types of gifts and gratuities are excluded from the $100 annual gift limit?
cards.back: Occasional business entertainment (meals, tickets) when a rep of the giving firm accompanies the recipient; reminder advertising items with the firm's logo (pens, mouse pads); and gifts for life events (weddings, births, retirement). All must be reasonable.

cards.front: A mutual fund wholesaler mails an RR two tickets, valued at $150, to every home game of the RR's favorite team. Allowed?
cards.back: No. This violates the gift rule. It exceeds $100, it is not occasional, and the wholesaler will not be present, so it does not qualify as business entertainment.

cards.front: Under MSRB Rule G-37, what is the consequence if a municipal firm, an MFP, or a firm-controlled PAC makes a political contribution to an issuer official?
cards.back: The municipal firm is prohibited from engaging in negotiated municipal securities underwriting or financial advisory business with that issuer for 2 years after the contribution.

cards.front: Municipal Finance Professional (MFP)
cards.back: An associated person of a FINRA member engaged in municipal securities underwriting, trading, sales, financial advisory, research, or investment advice, including those communicating with public investors. Excludes persons whose work is solely retail sales to individuals or clerical/ministerial.

cards.front: What is the de minimis political contribution exemption under MSRB Rule G-37 for MFPs?
cards.back: An MFP may contribute up to $250 per election to any candidate for whom the MFP is eligible to vote without triggering the 2-year ban. The de minimis exemption does NOT apply to contributions made by the firm itself (a firm cannot vote).

cards.front: A municipal firm previously made political contributions to a local issuer's officials. The issuer now solicits competitive bids for a new bond underwriting. May the firm participate?
cards.back: Yes. MSRB Rule G-37's 2-year ban applies only to negotiated underwritings and financial advisory work, not to competitive bid underwritings. The firm may submit a bid.

cards.front: Why does the MSRB rely on FINRA to enforce Rule G-37?
cards.back: The MSRB writes rules for the municipal securities industry but has no enforcement authority. Enforcement of MSRB rules against broker-dealers is carried out by FINRA.
